blocks.text: Have you ever wondered what makes up the air we breathe every day? Let's explore the composition of air and how oxygen, a vital component, is prepared in the laboratory.

blocks.markdown: Air is a mixture of gases that surrounds us. The composition of dry air by volume is approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases, including argon, carbon dioxide, and trace amounts of other noble gases.

blocks.title: Definition of Air
blocks.text: Air is a mixture of gases, primarily composed of nitrogen and oxygen, with small amounts of other gases.

blocks.markdown: Oxygen is essential for life as it supports respiration in living organisms. It is also used in various industrial processes. In the laboratory, oxygen can be prepared by the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide using manganese(IV) oxide as a catalyst.

blocks.title: Laboratory Preparation of Oxygen
blocks.prompt: Describe the laboratory preparation of oxygen using hydrogen peroxide.

steps.text: Set up the apparatus with a conical flask connected to a delivery tube leading to an inverted gas jar filled with water.
Add manganese(IV) oxide to hydrogen peroxide in the flask. Oxygen gas will be produced and collected over water.

blocks.answer: Oxygen is prepared by decomposing hydrogen peroxide with manganese(IV) oxide as a catalyst, collecting the gas over water.

blocks.markdown: To test for oxygen, place a glowing splint into the gas. If the splint relights, the gas is confirmed to be oxygen.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that oxygen supports combustion, which is why a glowing splint relights in its presence.

points: Dry air is composed of approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases.
Oxygen can be prepared in the lab by decomposing hydrogen peroxide with manganese(IV) oxide.
Oxygen supports combustion, which is a key test for its presence.
